newsitem.title: UK: SNOOKER-HENDRY WON, DAVIS LOSING, O'SULLIVAN LOST.
newsitem.headline: SNOOKER-HENDRY WON, DAVIS LOSING, O'SULLIVAN LOST.

text.p: Titleholder Stephen Hendry raced through the final five frames for a 13-8 victory over Mark Williams on Saturday to stay on course for a modern-era record seventh world snooker title.
But another six-times champion, Steve Davis, dropped the first five frames to Irishman Ken Doherty and trailed 6-2 after the opening session of their best-of-25-frame second round contest.
Earlier in the day, Englishman Ronnie O'Sullivan, who made a maximum 147 break in the first round, was knocked out 13-12 by tough Welshman Darren Morgan
Hendry resumed in the morning at 8-8 with Williams, who had beaten him 9-2 in the British Open final earlier this month.
Williams would have been in a much stronger position but for wasting several good chances in the first two sessions, during which he led 4-1 6-4 and 8-6 only to be pegged back to level each time.
But the 28-year-old Scottish holder ruthlessly enforced his superiority when it mattered to earn his quarter-final place against Morgan.
Davis, the 10th seed, found it tough going against the unpredictable seventh seed Doherty and made only 56 points during the first five frames, in three of which he did not score at all.

Morgan trailed 9-7 when he resumed against O'Sullivan but quickly levelled as the Englishman failed to sink a ball. Morgan made breaks of 116 and 59 as he managed to keep the O'Sullivan off the table for long periods.

Leading 11-10, there was real drama as Morgan potted a difficult long black to force a respot then, after losing the toss, doubled the black down the table into the corner pocket to move 12-10 in front and one frame from victory.
O'Sullivan showed his fighting spirit by winning the next two 84-44 and 89-39 but Morgan was not to be denied and compiled a painstaking 84 without reply to clinch victory.
Morgan, whose mother died late last year, broke down in tears afterwards.
O'Sullivan said: "On the whole Darren played much better than I did. It would have been an injustice had I won.".
The Welshman plays Hendry in the quarter-finals and on this form could pose a real threat.
French-Canadian Alain Robidoux extended his advantage from 5-3 to 11-7 against Englishman Stefan Mazrocis.
